title: Garlic Pork Skillet
seoTitle: Kielbasa Cabbage Potato Skillet | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: One-pan smoked sausage with cabbage and potatoes for ten
subtitle: One-pan smoked sausage with cabbage and potatoes for ten
description: Kielbasa slices sear with onion, then simmer with cabbage and potatoes until tender. Mustard and caraway finish the pan for a simple, filling one-pot meal.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Garlic Pork Skillet in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch pork. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Brown the kielbasa
steps.instruction: Sear kielbasa slices in a large skillet over medium-high heat 4–5 minutes until edges caramelize. Set aside. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 145°F with a 3-minute rest on an instant-read thermometer. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Start the potatoes
steps.instruction: Add onion and potatoes to the pan with a splash of broth. Cover and cook 12 minutes, stirring once, until potatoes begin to soften.

steps.title: Add cabbage and steam
steps.instruction: Nestle cabbage wedges into the pan, add remaining broth, cover, and cook 15 minutes until cabbage wilts and potatoes pierce easily.

steps.title: Combine and season
steps.instruction: Return kielbasa, stir in garlic, mustard, vinegar, caraway, and pepper. Cook uncovered 5 minutes until liquid mostly reduces. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F with a 3-minute rest. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Garlic Pork Skillet onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Serve from the skillet
steps.instruction: Taste for salt. Serve straight from the skillet or transfer to a hotel pan for buffet line. Target 145°F with a 3-minute rest at the thickest part before moving to the next batch. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Andouille or smoked turkey sausage works if kielbasa is not in the freezer.
A splash of beer instead of half the broth adds depth without complexity.
This reheats well—add broth when warming so potatoes do not dry out.
tonightSpread: Skillet served with rye bread and whole-grain mustard.
Quick vinegar slaw if you want a raw crunch side.
leftovers: Chop and fry into a breakfast hash with eggs.
Wrap in tortillas with sauerkraut for quick kielbasa tacos.
whyCrewsLikeIt: This is the meal you teach a probie first—hard to mess up, one pan, and everyone recognizes sausage and potatoes. Perfect when the crew is short on cooks.
mealPrepNotes: Slice kielbasa and potatoes uniform for even cooking. Use a lid to steam cabbage—dry pan burns before veg softens. Caraway is optional but classic.
